answer: Cross-embodiment continuity check: each agent must hold a continuous sensorimotor trace, its mirror of physical collisions and timing jitter, that a second instance cannot replay without divergence. Registries require the trace to match a grove of independent probes at random intervals, so cloning one identity yields detectable timing drift within hours. Reaching the summit of trust thus demands real hardware running in real time, and scaling to N identities costs N full robotic bodies plus continuous calibration labor.
